Sarcoidosis: Retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy associated with retroperitoneal fibrosis
Enlarged lymph nodes (up to 1.8 cm in short axis) were present along both pelvic sidewalls
Negative stains for acid-fast bacilli and fungi

top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient presents with non-caseating granulomatous lymphadenitis, retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, and enlarged lymph nodes, which are consistent with sarcoidosis. The negative stains for acid-fast bacilli and fungi also support this diagnosis. Additionally, the presence of bilateral basal pleural thickening is a common finding in sarcoidosis.
